properties.name: Solstice Advanced Materials (formerly Honeywell / Allied Chemical) — AWE Superfund Site
properties.source: EPA NPL / NCC Parcel Records (0607400002) / Honeywell-Solstice spin-off Oct. 2025
properties.note: NCC Parcel 0607400002 — 14.72 acres, Allied Corporation subdivision, 0 Off Philadelphia Pike, Claymont. As of Oct. 30, 2025, Honeywell completed the spin-off of its Advanced Materials division as Solstice Advanced Materials US Inc (Nasdaq: SOLS), which is now the listed contact on county parcel records for this property. The site remains on the EPA National Priorities List (Superfund). Solstice inherited environmental remediation liabilities from Honeywell as part of the spin-off; the Claymont AWE site traces directly to Allied Chemical's fluorine/specialty chemicals operations — the same business that became Solstice. Solstice's SEC filings acknowledge material environmental cleanup obligations. Residents and DNREC should confirm which entity now holds formal legal responsibility for site remediation.

properties.name: Evraz Claymont Steel — Former Steel Mill (closed 2015)
properties.source: EPA TRI / DNREC Title V / DNREC VCP
properties.note: Steel production at this site ended in 2015 after nearly a century of operations. The property and surrounding land remain contaminated with heavy metals, oils, and industrial byproducts from steel manufacturing. The site is subject to ongoing DNREC oversight. Permit violations and hazardous site conditions remain active concerns. Three large distribution warehouses — totaling over one million square feet — have since been built on and adjacent to the former mill property, bringing a new wave of diesel truck traffic and industrial noise to a neighborhood already burdened by decades of heavy industry.

properties.name: Pepsi Distribution Center — Former Steel Mill Site
properties.chemicals: Diesel exhaust (PM2.5, NOx, benzene), Engine noise
properties.note: Large distribution warehouse built directly on the former Evraz/Citisteel steel mill property — land that remains under DNREC oversight for contamination from nearly a century of steel production. Constant diesel truck traffic to and from this facility adds to Claymont's already 96th-percentile traffic exposure burden. Residents were not meaningfully consulted on the reuse of this contaminated industrial land for another high-truck-traffic use.

properties.name: Agile Cold Storage — Former Steel Mill Site
properties.chemicals: Diesel exhaust, Refrigerant emissions (ammonia or HFCs), 24-hr mechanical noise
properties.note: Refrigeration warehouse built on the former Evraz/Citisteel steel mill property. Refrigeration facilities operate 24 hours a day — meaning diesel truck arrivals, refrigeration compressor noise, and equipment vibration continue through overnight hours when residents are trying to sleep. Refrigerants used in cold storage (ammonia or hydrofluorocarbons) carry their own health and climate risks. This site adds a continuous noise and air quality burden on top of the existing industrial legacy of the property.

properties.name: Former Tri-State Mall — Vacant
properties.note: The former Tri-State Mall is currently vacant with no confirmed permits or approved reuse as of April 2026. CC4EJ is monitoring this site given its size and location in an already overburdened community. Any future industrial or high-traffic use of this property would add to a neighborhood already in the 96th percentile statewide for traffic and diesel exposure.

properties.name: Citisteel / Phoenix Steel Contamination Site (DE-0046)
properties.note: 343-acre former steel site at 4001 Philadelphia Pike. Steel production since 1917. 7 operable units under DNREC cleanup. Naamans Creek was relocated during operations. Adjacent to Delaware River and I-95/495.

properties.name: INEOS (formerly General Chemical) — Delaware Valley Works
properties.note: Major sulfuric acid plant; listed in UCS EJ for DE report

properties.name: I-95 / I-495 / Route 13 — Claymont Diesel Corridor
properties.source: DNREC / UCS report / CC4EJ listening session
properties.note: Community repeatedly identified being sandwiched between I-95 and I-495 as a primary air/noise concern (Sept. 2025 listening session, 47 attendees)

properties.name: Monroe Energy LLC — Trainer Refinery
properties.source: EPA TRI / EDF CEAM / DNREC VOC Study 2019
properties.chemicals: Benzene, Toluene, SO2, NOx, PM2.5, Hydrogen sulfide, VOCs
properties.de_implication: This refinery processes approximately 185,000 barrels of crude oil per day on the Delaware River, 3 miles from Claymont across the PA state line. DNREC's 2019 VOC Community Study was designed specifically to test whether emissions from this corridor reach Claymont residents. EDF's Chemical Exposure and Action Map (CEAM) identifies it as a major contributor to cumulative toxic exposure along the Delaware River. Delaware residents have no legal standing in PA air permit proceedings for this facility despite breathing the same air.

properties.name: Energy Transfer Marcus Hook Complex
properties.source: EPA TRI / DNREC VOC Study 2019 / CC4EJ listening session Sept. 2025
properties.chemicals: Methane, Propane, Ethylene, Butane, Benzene, VOCs
properties.de_implication: One of the largest LNG export facilities on the East Coast, located directly on the Delaware River in Marcus Hook — the facility most frequently named by Claymont residents as their top air concern at CC4EJ's Sept. 2025 listening session (47 attendees). Flaring events release VOCs and combustion byproducts. PCIST's 20-year cancer study documents Marcus Hook Borough residents — living adjacent to this complex — face laryngeal cancer at 280% above the US rate. Prevailing winds carry emissions northwest toward Claymont.

properties.name: Braskem America — Marcus Hook
properties.de_implication: Braskem operates the largest polypropylene production facility in the Americas at Marcus Hook. 1,3-Butadiene is a known human carcinogen (IARC Group 1) associated with leukemia and lymphoma. The facility is 2.5 miles from Claymont. PCIST cancer data for Marcus Hook Borough — immediately adjacent — shows liver cancer at 168% above the US rate and pediatric liver cancer at 2,362% above the US rate, consistent with long-term exposure to the compounds released at this and nearby facilities.

properties.name: Lubrizol Corp — Delaware River
properties.de_implication: EDF's Chemical Exposure and Action Map (CEAM) identifies Lubrizol as accounting for approximately 23% of cumulative chemical exposure burden in the Delaware River corridor. Acrylonitrile (IARC Group 2B) and formaldehyde (IARC Group 1 — known human carcinogen) are the primary releases. Formaldehyde is associated with leukemia and nasopharyngeal cancer. These compounds are part of the same chemical burden affecting the airshed serving Claymont, DE, 4 miles across the state line.

properties.name: Valtris Specialty Chemicals — Delaware River Plant
properties.de_implication: Valtris manufactures DEHP and related phthalate plasticizers on the Delaware River in Marcus Hook. DEHP is an endocrine-disrupting compound classified as a probable human carcinogen by EPA and a Substance of Very High Concern under EU REACH. EDF's CEAM tool lists this facility as a named contributor to cumulative toxic exposure in the Delaware River corridor — the same regional airshed as Claymont, DE. Phthalates are associated with developmental and reproductive harm, adding to the cumulative burden on communities along this corridor.

properties.name: ReWorld (formerly Covanta) Chester Incinerator
properties.chemicals: Dioxins/furans, Lead, Cadmium, Mercury, PM2.5, NOx, Hydrogen chloride
properties.de_implication: The largest trash-to-energy incinerator in the United States, burning approximately 3,500 tons of municipal solid waste per day from multiple counties. Chester, PA — a majority-Black city 8 miles north of Claymont — has among the highest cancer rates in Pennsylvania, substantially driven by this facility. Dioxins and furans released during incineration are persistent organic pollutants that travel significant distances, contributing to regional dioxin background levels in the Delaware Valley airshed that affects Claymont and the broader NCC industrial corridor.

properties.name: Evonik Corp — Marcus Hook
properties.chemicals: Hydrogen peroxide, Organic peroxides, Specialty chemical intermediates
properties.de_implication: Evonik manufactures specialty chemicals including organic peroxides at Marcus Hook, PA, 2.5 miles from Claymont. Organic peroxides are reactive oxidizers that contribute to ground-level ozone formation — the same ozone that worsens asthma and lung disease in downwind communities. Claymont residents are breathing air from a corridor where multiple facilities are simultaneously releasing ozone precursors, adding up to a burden no single permit review captures.

properties.name: Mexichem Specialty Resins (Vestolit) — Marcus Hook
properties.chemicals: Vinyl chloride, Ethylene dichloride, PVC resin dust, VOCs
properties.de_implication: EDF's Chemical Exposure and Action Map identifies this facility as a named contributor to cumulative chemical exposure in the Delaware River corridor. Vinyl chloride is a known human carcinogen (IARC Group 1) — the same compound linked to liver angiosarcoma, a rare cancer documented at elevated rates in communities near PVC manufacturing sites. Located 3.5 miles from Claymont in the same industrial cluster that Claymont residents identified as their top air concern.

properties.name: Chemours Chambers Works — Deepwater, NJ
properties.source: EPA TRI / EPA PFAS enforcement / Delaware River Basin Commission
properties.chemicals: PFOA (C8), GenX (HFPO-DA), PFOS, Fluorinated intermediates, HF, VOCs
properties.de_implication: Chambers Works is one of the most significant PFAS contamination sources in the United States and is located directly across the Delaware River from Delaware. For decades, DuPont (now Chemours) released C8 (PFOA) from this plant into air and water — contaminating the Delaware River, which serves as drinking water source for millions including Delaware communities. The Delaware River Basin Commission has found PFAS contamination throughout the watershed. This facility and Chemours Edge Moor in DE (same company) form a two-state PFAS contamination corridor along the river. PFAS are associated with thyroid disease, kidney and testicular cancer, immune suppression, and developmental harm.

properties.name: Paulsboro Refining Company — Paulsboro, NJ
properties.chemicals: Benzene, Toluene, Xylene, SO2, NOx, PM2.5, Hydrogen sulfide
properties.de_implication: The Paulsboro Refinery sits on the New Jersey side of the Delaware River, directly across from the Chester/Marcus Hook industrial corridor. Refinery emissions from both banks of the Delaware travel with wind — creating a corridor where communities on either shore face exposure from sources they cannot regulate or vote on. New Castle County, DE sits at the downriver end of this corridor. PCIST cancer data for Marcus Hook Borough (across from Paulsboro) shows lung cancer at 129% above the US rate — a pattern consistent with long-term exposure from both PA and NJ refinery operations.

properties.name: LANXESS Corp — Logan Township, NJ
properties.chemicals: Chlorinated organics, Rubber chemicals, Specialty intermediates, VOCs
properties.de_implication: LANXESS operates a specialty chemical facility in Logan Township, NJ, contributing chlorinated organic compounds and VOCs to the Delaware River airshed. Logan Township sits midway between Philadelphia and Wilmington along the NJ shore — its emissions mix with those from PA and DE facilities to create the cumulative chemical burden that no single state's environmental agency has full visibility into. New Castle County, DE is downwind of this corridor under common weather patterns.

properties.name: Infineum USA — Paulsboro, NJ
properties.chemicals: Petroleum distillates, Organic sulfur compounds, Zinc compounds, VOCs
properties.de_implication: Infineum manufactures fuel and lubricant additive packages at Paulsboro, NJ on the Delaware River. Organic sulfur compounds and petroleum distillates released during production contribute to particulate formation and ground-level ozone in the Delaware Valley airshed. Located on the NJ shore directly across from the Marcus Hook/Chester PA industrial cluster — together these two banks of the Delaware form one of the most industrially dense river corridors on the East Coast, with Delaware communities at the downstream end.
